memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They made the plate, the sacred emblem, out of pure gold and engraved on it, like an inscription on a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD. Then they fastened a blue cord to it to attach it to the turban, as the Lord commanded Moses." - Exod 39:30-31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A gold plate on the priest's forehead, engraved with three words: HOLY TO THE LORD.

It was the first thing anyone saw when they looked at him, and the last thing they would forget. His identity was written across his face.

The earlier instruction explains why it mattered: it was worn so that guilt might be borne and the offerings accepted before the Lord (Exod 28:38). Even Israel's worship was imperfect and needed covering. The plate declared that the priest — and through him the people — belonged wholly to God.

We should feel the weight of that. Our best worship is stained. Our purest prayers are mixed. If acceptance depended on the quality of what we offer, none of us would qualify.

But Christ our great High Priest is truly and perfectly holy, and He presents us to God. He offers us as a gift, and we are accepted in Him (Eph 1:6). Peter says we offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ (1 Pet 2:5) — through Him, not on our own merit.

And this is now our identity too. You are a holy nation, God's special possession (1 Pet 2:9). Not because we achieved it. Because He said it.

What is written across your forehead — what do people learn about you first?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Whose you are, or what you do — which comes first in how you see yourself?
2. Do you believe your imperfect worship is accepted in Christ?
3. What would change if "holy to the Lord" defined your day?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I belong to You. Thank You that my imperfect offerings are accepted because of Jesus. Amen.
